rounds.text: Despite headline growth metrics, Talbros Engineering Ltd carries notable financial friction and risk highlighted by its cash burn and rising debt profile [E36, E39]. Free cash flow dropped to Rs -8 Cr in Mar 2026, and total borrowings increased to Rs 148 Cr from Rs 132 Cr a year earlier, showing that reported profits are not translating cleanly into unencumbered cash [E36, E39]. Compounded profit growth over the last 3 years has stalled to just 1%, running well behind historical rates [E20]. Furthermore, the yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends are explicitly flagged as inconsistent [E32, E33], while the dividend payout has remained low at 7.64% of profits over the last 3 years [E58]. Compounded share price growth over the same 3-year horizon has likewise slowed to a negligible 2% [E24]. Finally, the stock carries extreme historical downside vulnerability, featuring a worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -85.2% and an annualized volatility of 58.2% [E52, E53]. Conceded: [E44].

While the bear points to a free cash flow of Rs -8 Cr and rising borrowings to Rs 148 Cr [E36, E39], this coincides with a massive 350.0% surge in capital-work-in-progress to Rs 18 Cr, representing productive growth spend underway rather than operational distress [E40]. Furthermore, operating cash flow remains robust at Rs 45 Cr, fully backing reported profits with a 1.55x cash conversion ratio [E34, E35, E37]. Conceded: [E36]. Although 3-year profit growth slowed to 1% [E20], trailing twelve-month profit growth has rebounded dramatically to 46% alongside a 20% jump in sales [E17, E21]. The inconsistent margin trend [E32, E33] is offset by a recent quarter operating margin expansion of +1 percentage point year-over-year [E31], while strong momentum is validated by an 84 relative-strength rating and an institutional rules-based score of 91 out of 100 [E50, E59]. Conceded: [E52, E53].
